newsitem.title: FRANCE: RENAULT TO CUT 2,764 JOBS IN FRANCE IN '97.
newsitem.headline: RENAULT TO CUT 2,764 JOBS IN FRANCE IN '97.

text.p: French carmaker Renault SA expects to cut 2,764 jobs in France this year and transfer 1,032 positions within the group, a source close to the company said on Tuesday.
Renault announced last Thursday it will close a Belgian assembly plant at Vilvoorde, near Brussels, in July with the loss of 3,100 jobs.
The news sparkeed widespread protests in Belgium and France.
A Renault spokeswoman declined to comment but said the central staff committee would be meeting on March 13 to discuss an "employment plan" in France.
The company's trade unions confirmed they had been notified on Tuesday of the job cuts.

The programme would include "both a labour restructuring with internal transfers and the elimination of posts, as well as measures aimed at youth employment, with new recruitment to make up for early retirements," the Renault spokeswoman said.
Renault unions have called a one-hour strike on Friday in all plants in France, Belgium and Spain to protest against the shutdown of the Belgian factory.
"We hope this is the beginning of a long period of labour struggle at Renault all over Europe," Daniel Richter of the pro-Socialist CFDT union said on Europe 1 radio on Tuesday.
